reviewers.summary: The child process, time limit, and bounded output are implemented. The memory limit is not hard-enforced on Windows, leaving a reachable path for a single-page PDF to exceed the limit during parsing.

findingList.message: The worker has no OS-enforced memory cap on Windows. Add a Job Object limit so a rapid allocation spike cannot exceed the 512 MB limit before the sampling checks run.

evidence.codePathTraced: On Windows, CreateStartInfo does not apply an OS memory cap; Supervise checks WorkingSetBytes only between 25 ms waits, while ExtractText checks the worker's working set only before parsing and between pages.
evidence.failureScenario: On a Windows host, a crafted single-page PDF causes a rapid decompression allocation spike during page parsing. The worker can exceed 512 MB before either working-set check runs, so the host can be exhausted despite the acceptance criterion requiring a hard memory limit where the platform offers one.

reviewers.summary: The tests cover the main parser and supervision scenarios. The AC-4 test can pass even when the worker directory is writable.

findingList.message: The AC-4 test does not verify that the worker's working directory is read-only; it only checks the configured path.

evidence.codePathTraced: The AC-4 test creates a writable temporary directory, passes it to CreateStartInfo, and checks only that the configured working-directory path matches. It never checks the permissions Parse applies to its working directory.
evidence.failureScenario: If the read-only permission setup in Parse is removed, this test still passes because its temporary directory remains writable. The read-only working-directory behavior in AC-4 is therefore not verified.

reviewers.summary: The parser runs in a child process, but on Windows its memory limit is sampled only outside the PDF parsing operation. A crafted single-page PDF can cause an unchecked allocation spike.

findingList.message: The Windows worker has no hard memory cap, and its working-set checks do not run during PdfDocument.Open. A crafted PDF can exceed the intended limit before the worker can detect it.

evidence.codePathTraced: On Windows, the worker has no job object memory cap. Its working-set checks run before PdfDocument.Open and between pages, not during PDF parsing.
evidence.failureScenario: An attacker submits a crafted PDF that causes PdfDocument.Open to allocate hundreds of megabytes while processing a single page. The worker can exceed the 512 MB limit before another check runs, exhausting memory on the service host.
